name: whatsapp-e2e
description: End-to-end tests driving the real MCP server against the real API. Ships nowhere.
//: No `build` script on purpose: `pnpm -r run build` skips a package that lacks one, and nothing consumes this package's output.
//scripts: `build:deps` builds this package's workspace dependencies — the SDK, whose `dist/` both product packages compile against. `whatsapp-api` and `whatsapp-mcp` are consumed as TypeScript *source* through their `src/**` subpaths (neither publishes types, and neither has an `exports` map that would stop it), which is what lets an e2e test inject a fake Baileys socket into the real connection.
//devDependencies: Every dependency is a dev one: nothing imports this package and it ships nowhere. `whatsapp-api` and `whatsapp-mcp` are here so the pair under test is the real one, and `baileys` is here for the `WASocket` type the fake socket satisfies. Keeping all three off `whatsapp-mcp`'s own manifest is what keeps `pnpm --filter whatsapp-mcp why baileys` empty (Global Constraint 1).
